dedupe_keys.name: tceq hurricane harvey 2017 after action review public water systems and wastewater plants

description: This after action review by the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality captures the agency's response to Hurricane Harvey, which made landfall on 25 August 2017 as a Category 4 storm and stalled, dropping more than 19 trillion gallons of rain. For water and wastewater it reports tracking 2,238 community water systems serving about 11 million people, of which 61 were offline or damaged at the peak between 31 August and 4 September, serving 222,821 people, and 1,743 wastewater plants serving about 10 million, of which 40 were offline or damaged on 7 September, serving 168,816 people; more than 200 systems issued boil-water notices and sewers overflowed. Assistance teams of state and EPA engineers worked 24-hour shifts with operators to restore service, and the report also covers debris sites, hazardous materials and staffing, ending with lessons passed forward. Coverage: 58 disaster-declared counties, one event. Access: a free PDF; the licence is not stated. Caveats: an agency self-review with counts, not asset-level data. It supports outage, restoration and emergency response modelling for water utilities, and relates to the TCEQ winter storm Uri after action review case study already in the catalogue.
